summary:
Round 4, test lane. THE DELTA IS ONE JAVADOC SENTENCE AND I PROVED THAT INDEPENDENTLY OF THE DIFF, twice. (a) Tree diff: round-3 staged tree 36fd2017 -> this index touches three files, and the only source file is CommitProtocolSimulationFlushSeqTest.java, 3 comment lines for 3. Widening to round-2 tree e63855ef -> now over sequencer/ingest/format/client/http gives ONE file, 9 lines for 9, all comment -- so CommitProtocolSimulation.java, the production-side driver, is byte-identical to what passed both roles at round 2 (sha 9f7022da on the index and in my tree). (b) Red records: check-tdd binding keys hash the declaration plus the file's non-test remainder with comments STRIPPED, so I recomputed both from the staged blob -- everyPodIssuesADenseSequenceFromZeroAndTwoPodsReachTheSameValue -> 76f89ea520c1e266baf7ac73b53a2f0733d6a7743e7639f75d769bd7a1f44fdd and noPodIdAndFlushSeqPairIsEverIssuedForTwoDifferentSegments -> 1464fedc331f77d217caef01cda74cb87f33879913d9798e7bf7dc4ef1bc9ebe -- and both equal the recorded sha256 in .harness/tdd/red.json byte for byte. GATE_SCOPE=full check-tdd: '2 new test(s), all observed failing first, unchanged since'. No executable token has moved since the red was observed.

THE SURVIVING JAVADOC CLAIM IS TRUE AND I MEASURED IT RATHER THAN CARRIED IT. Instrumented sweep over seeds 0..29 at ROUGH on the staged bytes: seedsWithSharedValue=19, seedsWithTwoOrMoreIssuingPods=19 -- equal, so 'on correct code the two coincide, measured at 19 of 30 seeds' is exact, not approximate. seedsAllPodsDense=30, seedsWithNonDensePod=0, totalIssued=211 > totalLanded=175, so no anti-vacuity guard is green for a trivial reason. 'Forces a shared value by construction' is sound as stated: density from zero means every issuing pod issues 0, so two issuing pods share 0 -- and the two counts coinciding at 19/19 is the measurement of exactly that implication, with no seed on either side of it.

NOTHING LOAD-BEARING WAS LOST, AND THE DELETION WAS THE RIGHT CALL. The deleted clause's only non-redundant content was 'and not a second discriminator ... rather than independent', which I measured FALSE at round 3 and re-measured false here: with the density assertion neutralised (replaced by assertThat(expected).isNotNull()) and the allocator keyed on a constant instead of the pod, the test still fails, on the shared-value assertion alone -- 'no seed had two pods reach the same flushSeq ... Expecting actual: 0 to be greater than: 0'. Everything true in the old clause (19 of 30, forced by construction, guard role) survives in the new one. I recommended not fixing it because it was a minor; the author deleted it because it was false and the sentence was already being edited. That was the better call and I withdraw the recommendation: review.sh's own cap message prescribes exactly this remedy -- 'if the last rounds have been finding prose rather than defects, the honest move is to DELETE the prose that keeps being wrong rather than correct it again' -- and I verified the replacement sentence in full, so it adds no unverified surface.

THE PIN STILL HOLDS ON THESE BYTES; I did not take round 2 on trust. Full revert of both allocator sites to the outcome counters (leader -> commits, zombie -> zombieWrites, the original defect) fails BOTH tests: ':76 seed 1 reissued pod1#0 for seg/zombie-23 after seg/2' and ':112 seed 0: pod pod2 must issue 0..n-1, expected [0, 1] but was [15, 16]'. A single fleet-wide per-attempt counter (allocator keyed on the constant "shared") leaves the uniqueness test GREEN and fails the density test at :112. :sequencer:test as a whole is BUILD SUCCESSFUL on the unmutated staged bytes.

THE baselines rounds:M4.10a ARGUMENT, checked clause by clause where it describes the tests. TRUE, verified: 'the code passed both roles at round 2 and has not changed since' (tree diff above; both round-2 verdicts are pass); 'the driver change was right in round 1' (round-1 tree 686f1fdeb already had nextFlushSeq.merge(pod, 1L, Long::sum) - 1 feeding both CommitRequests -- what was missing was the pin, not the value); 'both reviewers independently measured that it was UNPINNED' (both round-1 verdicts carry a major naming the fleet-wide per-attempt counter, reached independently); 'uniqueness is satisfied by a single fleet-wide per-attempt counter, so PER POD had no failing test; density 0..n-1 per pod is what kills it' (re-measured above, exactly this split); 'reverting only the request's flushSeq argument left the recording correct, the suite green, and the driver reissuing (pod1, 0) for two segments' (matches the round-1 finding record verbatim, including the pair and the whole-module green). ONE CLAUSE IS FALSE and is the minor below.

No assertion was weakened: the predicate text of both tests is unchanged since round 2 by the byte comparison above. Tier is unchanged and right (T1, in-memory store and simulated clock, no socket, no sleep, no fixed port, no system temp), @Timeout(120, SEPARATE_THREAD) present, the pair runs in ~1s.

findings.title: The rounds:M4.10a entry records the retracted claim as the correction: it says the overlap assertion was 'described as a discriminator when it is an anti-vacuity guard', which is the sentence this same commit deletes from the javadoc for being false
findings.surviving_mutation: Not a code mutation -- the tests are fully pinned and I re-measured every kill above. The falsifying measurement is the one that justifies the javadoc deletion: neutralise the density assertion (replace assertThat(pod.getValue())...isEqualTo(expected) with assertThat(expected).isNotNull()) and key the allocator on a constant instead of the pod. The test STILL FAILS, at CommitProtocolSimulationFlushSeqTest.java:124-127, 'no seed had two pods reach the same flushSeq ... Expecting actual: 0 to be greater than: 0'. The overlap assertion is therefore independently sufficient to kill a shared counter -- a discriminator as well as a guard -- so 'when it is an anti-vacuity guard', offered as the correction of 'described as a discriminator', is false. The sub-clause 'all deleted rather than rewritten' is also inaccurate for this third item: git diff e63855ef 36fd2017 shows round 3 REPLACED a true clause ('What separates the two is DENSITY and OVERLAP ... impossible under one shared counter') with the false one, and round 4's edit likewise adds new text ('on correct code the two coincide') rather than only cutting.
findings.failure_scenario: baselines/review.txt is the durable lessons record, read without the code beside it, and this entry is the argued exception that authorises rounds 3 and 4 -- so its account of why those rounds happened is the whole basis for the exception. As staged it teaches a future session two wrong things. First, that the shared-value assertion in this test discriminates nothing, when it independently kills the single fleet-wide counter; someone later tightening or trimming this test would believe removing it costs only vacuity protection, when it costs one of two independent kills of the mutation the row exists to exclude. Second, that round 3 was three clean deletions of pre-existing false claims -- which is the flattering version. The third was a rewrite that ADDED a false claim, and that added claim is the entire reason round 4 exists; the entry's own thesis, 'all deleted rather than rewritten ... because a deletion cannot add a claim', is falsified by the one instance it is citing. The error's direction is safe -- it understates test strength and cannot ship a bug -- which is why this is minor and not major, and it is the same fact I raised as a minor at round 3, so the severity is consistent. Provenance, for whoever fixes it: the clause inherits its error from the round-2 production reviewer's F8, which reasoned only over CORRECT code ('density forces every pod's sequence to start at 0, so ... identical by construction') and concluded the assertion 'discriminates nothing' -- true about the correct path, false about the mutant path, where the density premise is exactly what fails. Remedy, if any: DELETE the third item and say round 3 replaced a true clause with a false one, which round 4 removed. Do not open round 5 for it -- review.sh's own cap message says the honest move on prose that keeps being wrong is deletion, and rule 11 lets this land in the commit body.
